features.name: Dominant Communicative Purpose
features.question: What is the single primary job the post performs for its reader?
features.detection_method: Identify the activity receiving the most structural space and closure emphasis: understanding, doing, evaluating, adopting, learning news, hearing a guest, reviewing past material, or browsing selections.

features.name: Purpose Singularity
features.question: How many co-equal purposes does the post pursue?
values: dominant purpose with one secondary purpose
dominant purpose with two secondary purposes
features.detection_method: Compare whether education, instruction, persuasion, reporting, conversion, or curation receive independent structural space and closing emphasis.

features.name: Secondary Purpose Mix
features.question: Which secondary purposes materially shape the post in addition to its main purpose?
features.detection_method: Select every purpose supported by a dedicated section, repeated framing, product bridge, CTA, or explicit reader invitation.

features.name: Change Requested of Reader
features.question: What kind of change does the post primarily seek from the reader?
values: contact or buy from a provider
features.detection_method: Inspect the conclusion, imperatives, recommended next steps, and stated consequences of following the advice.

features.name: Incumbent Contrast Type
features.question: What contrast most strongly carries the post's argument?
features.detection_method: Identify the recurring before-versus-after pair in headings, transitions, examples, and conclusion.

features.name: Purpose Declaration Location
features.question: Where is the post's purpose first made explicit?
features.detection_method: Locate the first direct statement of what the article is for, rather than merely the first mention of its topic.

features.name: Primary Reader Role
features.question: What role does the post primarily assign to the reader?
features.detection_method: Infer the role from direct address, requested actions, assumed authority, and the kinds of choices the reader is asked to make.

features.name: Promised Outcome Type
features.question: What is the main outcome the reader is promised?
features.detection_method: Code the outcome named or implied by the headline, lede, subheadings, and final paragraph.

features.name: Outcome Explicitness
features.question: How explicitly does the post name what the reader will gain?
values: repeated as an explicit promise across the post
features.detection_method: Look for formulations such as 'you will learn,' 'by the end,' 'this guide helps you,' stated payoff headlines, and repeated outcome language.

features.name: Payoff First-Promise Location
features.question: Where is the reader payoff first promised?
features.detection_method: Locate the first text span that states or unmistakably signals what the reader will receive.

features.name: Success Criterion Visibility
features.question: How does the post indicate that the reader will know the guidance worked?
features.detection_method: Identify whether success is defined through a takeaway, test, score, threshold, checklist completion, output artifact, appointment, consultation, or purchase.

features.name: Decision Conditionality
features.question: How does the post frame the applicability of its recommendation?
features.detection_method: Inspect whether the article gives one answer for everyone, an answer with exceptions, if-then options, audience segments, or a clinician/provider handoff.

features.name: Reader Agency Level
features.question: What role does the post assign the reader in reaching the promised outcome?
features.detection_method: Assess direct address, expected skills, requested actions, and whether success depends on reader execution, organizational coordination, or provider engagement.

features.name: Success Criterion Visibility
features.question: How visibly does the post indicate how readers will know the advice has worked?
features.detection_method: Look for takeaways, measurable targets, diagnostic checks, threshold rules, validation steps, or stated signs of success.

features.name: Content Format
features.question: What is the post's primary formal structure?
features.detection_method: Classify the dominant organizing unit: sections, numbered items, questions, alternatives, evidence report, interview turns, cases, curated entries, or conversion modules.

features.name: Primary Organizing Unit
features.question: What repeated unit structures the body of the post?
features.detection_method: Identify the repeated body pattern rather than the overall genre label.

features.name: Navigation and Resource Density
features.question: What kind of page-level support extends the article beyond prose headings?
values: table, chart, code, or comparison artifact
conversion furniture such as forms, demos, downloads, or signup modules
features.detection_method: Inspect visible page furniture, tables, embedded code, charts, links, resource modules, forms, downloads, and conversion components.

features.name: Answer Timing
features.question: When does the post deliver its central answer or recommendation?
features.detection_method: Locate the first unambiguous answer to the core title question or problem statement.

features.name: Format Signaling Location
features.question: How is the format signaled to the reader?
features.detection_method: Check whether labels such as guide, FAQ, steps, report, interview, roundup, or list appear in title, opening, early headings, or only become apparent later.

features.name: Format-Purpose Alignment
features.question: How closely does the format support the post's dominant purpose?
features.detection_method: Compare the implied promise of the format with the actual work performed; for example, assess whether a guide genuinely instructs or mostly sells.

features.name: Supporting Artifact Type
features.question: Which supporting artifact types materially contribute to the post's payoff?
features.detection_method: Select every artifact that does more than decorate the page and instead supports evaluation, implementation, trust, or conversion.

features.name: Commercial Integration Level
features.question: How centrally is a named brand, product, provider, or commercial category integrated into the article's resolution?
features.detection_method: Track named brand references, their explanatory role, recurrence, and whether the argument can resolve without them.

features.name: Commercial Bridge Placement
features.question: Where does the first substantive commercial bridge appear?
features.detection_method: Find the first point where a brand or provider is positioned as an answer rather than merely named incidentally.

features.name: Section Sequence Pattern
features.question: What is the dominant sequence of section jobs across the article?
values: trend or list inventory to CTA
question to answer to next step
features.detection_method: Map the dominant job of consecutive major sections and choose the sequence that best matches the article's structural progression.

features.name: Payoff Restatement at Close
features.question: Does the conclusion restate the reader's promised benefit or success condition?
features.detection_method: Compare the closing language with the opening promise, title claim, or stated intended outcome.

features.name: Professional Handoff
features.question: Does the article direct the reader to an external professional decision-maker or specialist as part of success?
features.detection_method: Look for instructions to consult a clinician, lawyer, advisor, technician, regulator, specialist, or qualified service provider before or after reader action.

features.name: Action Packaging
features.question: How are recommended reader actions packaged?
features.detection_method: Inspect whether actions are abstract, modular, conditional, sequenced, controlled through roles and verification, or tied to specific interface operations.

features.name: Verification Loop Presence
features.question: Does the post require readers to verify, measure, test, monitor, or reassess the result of its recommended action?
features.detection_method: Look for explicit validation, thresholds, audits, monitoring, testing, comparison against baseline, self-checks, or post-action review.

features.name: Commercial Solution Placement
features.question: Where does the first substantive branded product, provider, or commercial solution enter the argument?
features.detection_method: Locate the first mention that materially links a named brand, provider, or commercial category to solving the reader's problem.

features.name: Conclusion Function
features.question: What is the primary job of the ending?
features.detection_method: Classify the final substantive paragraph or module by what it asks the reader to retain or do.

features.name: Recap Behavior
features.question: How does the post revisit its promised payoff near the end?
features.detection_method: Compare the ending with the opening promise and identify whether it restates the payoff, summarizes content, repeats a rule, reconstructs a process, or shifts directly to a pitch.

features.name: Answer-First Versus Suspense-First Opening
features.question: Does the opening tell readers the recommended answer before developing the problem?
features.detection_method: Examine the title and first two paragraphs for whether the preferred answer appears before the diagnostic buildup.

features.name: Closing Payoff Behavior
features.question: How does the post handle the reader payoff at the close?
features.detection_method: Inspect the final substantive section and determine whether it recaps the promised value, introduces new material, converts, redirects, or ends abruptly.

features.name: Reader Naming Explicitness
features.question: How explicitly does the article name its intended reader?
features.detection_method: Inspect the title, introduction, and early headings for direct naming of roles, personas, industries, organization types, or a generic public.

features.name: Audience Breadth
features.question: How narrowly bounded is the intended audience?
features.detection_method: Assess the number and specificity of qualifying attributes attached to the target reader.

features.name: Reader Expertise Assumption
features.question: How much domain knowledge does the article assume before explaining its recommendations?
features.detection_method: Assess whether the article defines basic terms, assumes fluency with jargon, and expects readers to understand specialist tools or governance concepts.

features.name: Reader Role Framing
features.question: How does the article position the reader's primary role in relation to the problem?
features.detection_method: Identify the dominant implied reader job in directives, examples, and conclusions.

features.name: Situation Mirroring in Opening
features.question: Does the opening reflect the reader's likely lived situation before explaining the topic or solution?
features.detection_method: Examine the title and first two paragraphs for a recognizable reader circumstance, pain scene, or role-specific scenario.

features.name: Primary Reader Role
features.question: What primary role does the post construct for its reader?
features.detection_method: Identify the role that is most directly assigned decisions, responsibilities, or actions.

features.name: Audience Segmentation Basis
features.question: What primary criterion does the article use to divide readers into applicable groups?
features.detection_method: Record every segmentation dimension explicitly used to distinguish advice, examples, or recommendations.

features.name: Reader Agency Framing
features.question: What kind of action authority does the text assign to the reader?
features.detection_method: Identify the primary verbs directed at the reader, such as choose, configure, manage, coordinate, approve, audit, or invest.

features.name: Reader Situation Mirroring
features.question: Does the opening reflect the reader's likely lived situation before presenting advice?
features.detection_method: Look for second-person or persona-specific recognition such as a scenario, frustration, constraint, or familiar moment in the opening.

features.name: Audience Qualification Density
features.question: How extensively does the article specify who the advice is or is not for?
features.detection_method: Assess the frequency of if/when/unless clauses, fit criteria, exclusions, and segment-specific recommendations.

features.name: Primary Trigger Type
features.question: What makes the topic relevant to the reader now?
features.detection_method: Identify the main event, condition, or opportunity used to justify relevance in the title and opening.

features.name: Temporal Specificity
features.question: How specific are the article's relevance-related time references?
features.detection_method: Assess the precision of dates, hours, weeks, quarters, seasons, or specified event windows.

features.name: Trigger Time Anchor
features.question: How is the trigger temporally framed?
features.detection_method: Inspect dates, seasons, quarters, deadlines, recurring cadences, historical references, and future-oriented language.

features.name: Urgency Construction
features.question: How strongly does the article present action as time-sensitive?
features.detection_method: Rate the strength of urgency cues such as now, before it is too late, immediate action, limited windows, deadlines, or imminent loss.

features.name: Staleness Acknowledgment
features.question: Does the article explicitly acknowledge that policy, platform, pricing, market, or product facts may change?
features.detection_method: Look for caveats concerning changing laws, interfaces, product capabilities, prices, eligibility rules, data, or market conditions.

features.name: Core Problem Form
features.question: How is the central problem first presented?
features.detection_method: Classify the earliest substantive presentation of the obstacle, uncertainty, failure, or decision.

features.name: Problem Placement
features.question: Where does the core problem first become explicit?
features.detection_method: Locate the first sentence that clearly identifies the obstacle, tension, or decision.

features.name: Problem Scale
features.question: At what level is the central problem primarily framed?
features.detection_method: Determine whether the problem concerns an individual's behavior, a task, a team process, an organization, or an external system.

features.name: Problem Framing Polarity
features.question: Is the problem framed as a deficit, a trade-off, or a missed opportunity?
features.detection_method: Review the diagnostic sections for the recurring logic that defines the problem.

features.name: False Default Challenged
features.question: Does the article explicitly portray an existing default practice as inadequate?
features.detection_method: Look for contrasts such as reactive versus proactive, legacy versus modern, manual versus automated, or generic versus tailored.

features.name: Problem Ownership Assignment
features.question: Who is portrayed as responsible for resolving the problem?
features.detection_method: Identify who receives the main imperatives, decision rights, or solution responsibilities.

features.name: Legacy Versus Modern Contrast
features.question: Does the article frame the core problem as dependence on an outdated or inferior legacy approach?
features.detection_method: Look for explicit old-versus-new, manual-versus-automated, reactive-versus-proactive, or traditional-versus-modern contrasts.

features.name: Problem Resolution Type Promised
features.question: What kind of resolution does the article imply it will provide?
features.detection_method: Determine the promised form of relief from the article's introduction, roadmap, headings, and conclusion.

features.name: Primary Stakes Domain
features.question: What is the primary kind of consequence attached to acting or failing to act?
features.detection_method: Identify the consequence domain emphasized most strongly in the introduction, body framing, or conclusion.

features.name: Stakes Escalation
features.question: Does the article escalate from a practical inconvenience to a larger strategic, financial, safety, or identity consequence?
features.detection_method: Mark present when the article explicitly moves from a small issue, such as delay or friction, to major loss, harm, compliance exposure, or strategic failure.

features.name: Product as Stakes Resolution
features.question: Is a named product, platform, provider, or service framed as necessary to resolve the article's stakes?
features.detection_method: Mark present when the named offering is presented as the practical answer to the diagnosed risk or missed opportunity.

features.name: Primary Stakes Domain
features.question: What is the most prominent domain of consequence?
features.detection_method: Identify the consequence domain emphasized most often or most strongly in opening and conclusion.

features.name: Stakes Valence
features.question: Does the article frame stakes as avoiding losses, gaining benefits, or both?
features.detection_method: Compare language about risk, failure, harm, loss, opportunity, growth, upside, and benefit.

features.name: Consequence Specificity
features.question: How concretely are consequences rendered?
features.detection_method: Assess whether consequences are vague, named, scenarized, or expressed using amounts, rates, deadlines, or thresholds.

features.name: Stake Horizon
features.question: What time horizon dominates the stated stakes?
features.detection_method: Identify whether consequences concern today's event, a current cycle, a project horizon, or enduring outcomes.

features.name: Stake Escalation Pattern
features.question: How does the article develop stakes after the opening?
features.detection_method: Trace whether consequences intensify, remain stable, or are deferred as sections progress.

features.name: Opening Hook Type
features.question: What primary rhetorical device opens the article?
features.detection_method: Classify the title lead and first paragraph according to the first substantive relevance-building device.

features.name: Hook-to-Reader Connection Speed
features.question: How quickly does the opening connect the hook to a specific reader problem or audience?
features.detection_method: Locate the first explicit connection from opening material to reader role, pain, or decision.

features.name: Hook-to-Reader Connection Speed
features.question: How quickly does the opening connect its hook to a named or implied reader need?
features.detection_method: Locate the first sentence that translates the hook into relevance for the reader's role, condition, or decision.

features.name: Opening Emotional Register
features.question: What emotional tone dominates the opening?
features.detection_method: Classify the dominant affect created by word choice, imagery, warnings, promises, and scenario framing.

features.name: Opening Scenario Realism
features.question: What kind of situation, if any, is used to make the opening concrete?
features.detection_method: Identify whether the opening includes a situation and classify its attribution and realism.

features.name: Opening Reader Question Invitation
features.question: Does the opening explicitly invite the reader to self-diagnose through a question or recognizable condition?
features.detection_method: Look for questions or conditional statements asking readers to recognize themselves, their team, or their current situation.

features.name: Opening Rhetorical Temperature
features.question: What dominant emotional temperature does the opening establish?
features.detection_method: Assess opening diction, evaluative language, metaphors, and predicted consequences.

features.name: Opening Relevance Devices
features.question: Which relevance devices appear in the opening?
features.detection_method: Mark all devices that occur in the title, deck, or first two paragraphs.

features.name: Applicability Qualification Type
features.question: What type of applicability condition is most explicitly stated?
features.detection_method: Identify the condition that most directly limits whether advice applies.

features.name: Exclusion Clarity
features.question: How clearly does the article state cases where its recommendation does not apply?
features.detection_method: Look for not-for-you language, contraindications, disqualifying conditions, and alternative paths.

features.name: Recommendation Conditionality
features.question: How conditional is the central recommendation?
features.detection_method: Assess whether recommendations apply uniformly or route readers by conditions, thresholds, and fit.

features.name: Solution Framing
features.question: How is the preferred solution related to the diagnosed problem?
features.detection_method: Assess whether the article presents alternatives neutrally, conditionally, or as inferior to a required solution.

features.name: Problem-Solution Bridge Type
features.question: What rhetorical bridge most often connects the problem to the recommendation?
features.detection_method: Identify the dominant logic immediately before the article begins recommending a solution.

features.name: Solution Pressure
features.question: How strongly does the article imply that readers should adopt its preferred solution?
features.detection_method: Assess modal verbs, comparative claims, imperatives, dismissal of alternatives, and CTA strength.

features.name: Commercial Resolution Mode
features.question: How does the article commercially resolve, if at all?
features.detection_method: Review product placement and the final section for brand-driven next steps.

features.name: Reader Agency Distribution
features.question: Which parties are presented as necessary to solve the problem?
features.detection_method: Mark all actors assigned meaningful action, approval, implementation, or validation responsibility.

features.name: Trigger Framing Polarity
features.question: Is the trigger framed primarily as danger, opportunity, or both?
features.detection_method: Identify whether relevance rests on avoiding harm, capturing upside, both, or simply understanding a context.

features.name: Operational Timing Guidance
features.question: Does the article translate relevance into a specific operational time to act?
features.detection_method: Look for instructions such as before listing, during onboarding, within 24 hours, before an event, after a trigger, or at a stated cadence.

features.name: Primary Flow Archetype
features.question: What main sequence organizes the article's argument or instruction?
features.detection_method: Identify the dominant relationship between major sections, not isolated subsections.

features.name: Opening Entry Move
features.question: How does the article enter its subject before the main body begins?
features.detection_method: Inspect the title, lead, and first substantive section for the first rhetorical function performed.

features.name: Opening Ramp Length
features.question: How much setup appears before the first substantive recommendation, case, step, answer, or repeated unit?
features.detection_method: Count introductory material before the first clearly substantive content unit.

features.name: Article Cohesion Model
features.question: How tightly do sections depend on one another to produce the article's conclusion?
features.detection_method: Assess whether sections must be read in sequence or can be consumed independently.

features.name: Legacy-versus-Modern Contrast
features.question: Does the article organize persuasion around replacing a legacy, reactive, rigid, or fragmented model with a modern, proactive, or integrated model?
features.detection_method: Look for a sustained old-model versus new-model contrast across the heading sequence or major sections.

features.name: Thesis Before First Unit
features.question: Does the opening state a clear governing claim or recommendation before the article begins its main repeated units?
features.detection_method: Check whether the preferred conclusion or central claim appears before the first main section, tip, case, or step.

features.name: Commercial Resolution Placement
features.question: Where does the commercial solution or branded next step enter the article's structural flow?
features.detection_method: Locate the first substantive brand or product bridge and assess whether it recurs through the article or is isolated.

features.name: Functional Stage Inventory
features.question: Which major functional stages are present in the article?
features.detection_method: Mark every stage that receives a distinct passage, section, or sustained rhetorical function.

features.name: Exception and Qualification Placement
features.question: Where are exceptions, caveats, edge cases, eligibility limits, or safety qualifications primarily located?
features.detection_method: Identify where the article says advice varies by condition, audience, jurisdiction, risk, timing, or implementation context.

features.name: Conclusion Form
features.question: What primary structural function does the conclusion perform?
features.detection_method: Inspect the final substantive section and classify its dominant function.

features.name: Final Resolution Target
features.question: What does the article ultimately present as the resolution to the reader's problem?
features.detection_method: Read the final recommendation and identify the object readers are asked to adopt, use, decide, consult, or pursue.

features.name: Diagnosis Placement
features.question: Where does the main problem diagnosis occur?
features.detection_method: Locate explicit statements of what is wrong, risky, insufficient, or difficult.

features.name: Definition-to-Application Relationship
features.question: How are definitions or foundational explanations positioned relative to application?
features.detection_method: Compare the placement of term explanations with steps, recommendations, or examples.

features.name: Evidence Stage Placement
features.question: Where is supporting evidence, case material, quotation, or proof primarily placed?
features.detection_method: Track the location of attributed examples, numbers, cases, quotations, or research references.

features.name: Conclusion Behavior
features.question: How does the article primarily end?
features.detection_method: Classify the final substantive section or final two paragraphs by dominant function.

features.name: Editorial-to-CTA Separation
features.question: How clearly is commercial or next-step material separated from editorial guidance?
features.detection_method: Inspect whether the article shifts visibly from advice to promotion, contact, download, demo, or purchase language.

features.name: Primary Repeated Building Block
features.question: What is the dominant recurring unit used to build the article body?
features.detection_method: Identify the unit repeated across most body sections, headings, or paragraphs.

features.name: Main Unit Count
features.question: How many primary repeated units make up the article body?
features.detection_method: Count main steps, cases, tips, questions, profiles, or equivalent repeated sections.

features.name: Repeated Unit Uniformity
features.question: How uniform are the repeated units in length, depth, and internal composition?
features.detection_method: Compare unit lengths, subhead structure, evidence density, and action detail.

features.name: Within-Unit Template
features.question: What sequence most commonly appears inside a repeated unit?
features.detection_method: Inspect at least three repeated units and identify the most frequent internal progression.

features.name: Typical Within-Unit Sequence
features.question: What sequence most commonly appears inside a primary repeated unit?
features.detection_method: Inspect multiple units and choose the most recurrent internal progression.

features.name: Examples as Structural Units
features.question: How are examples used structurally in the article?
features.detection_method: Assess whether examples are occasional support, recurring hypothetical units, named cases, worked demonstrations, or the main unit structure.

features.name: Heading-to-Unit Alignment
features.question: How closely do headings correspond to the article's actual repeated units?
features.detection_method: Compare headings with the boundaries of tips, cases, steps, questions, or profiles.

features.name: Embedded Supporting Artifact Types
features.question: What supporting artifacts are embedded or visibly included in the article body or page?
features.detection_method: Mark all artifacts that visibly supplement prose beyond ordinary headings and paragraphs.

features.name: Primary Ordering Principle
features.question: What principle determines the order of the article's main units?
features.detection_method: Compare the relationship between successive headings and determine the dominant ordering logic.

features.name: Ordering Announced to Reader
features.question: Does the article explicitly announce how sections, steps, phases, or categories are ordered?
features.detection_method: Look for language such as 'Step One,' 'three phases,' 'first,' 'next,' 'by priority,' or an explicit roadmap.

features.name: Transition Mechanics
features.question: How are major sections connected?
features.detection_method: Examine the end of one section and start of the next for connective sentences, causal links, sequencing markers, or abrupt cuts.

features.name: Reader Reorientation Frequency
features.question: How often does the article restate where the reader is in the process or why the next section matters?
features.detection_method: Count roadmap reminders, recap bridges, 'now that' transitions, and explicit statements of the next reader task.

features.name: Dependency Explicitness
features.question: How explicitly does the article state that one action, phase, or section depends on another?
features.detection_method: Track terms such as 'before,' 'after,' 'only once,' 'then,' 'next,' 'prerequisite,' and explicit gates.

features.name: Conditional Routing Model
features.question: How does the article route readers to different recommendations?
features.detection_method: Identify whether recommendations vary according to reader conditions, scores, roles, symptoms, scale, or constraints.

features.name: Comparison Architecture
features.question: How are alternatives, options, or competing approaches organized?
features.detection_method: Inspect whether alternatives receive parallel treatment and how the article resolves the comparison.

features.name: Action Packaging Mode
features.question: How is practical guidance packaged?
features.detection_method: Identify whether actions are free-standing, conditional, sequential, diagnostic, interface-specific, or mostly absent.

features.name: Procedure Granularity
features.question: At what level of detail are the article's practical instructions specified?
features.detection_method: Assess the presence of named artifacts, thresholds, scripts, timing, tools, decision gates, and success checks.

features.name: Conditional Routing Density
features.question: How central are if-then fit rules, eligibility conditions, or branching recommendations to the article?
features.detection_method: Count and assess the structural importance of conditional recommendations such as 'choose X if Y' or 'avoid X when Y.'

features.name: Cadence as a Structural Component
features.question: How does recurring time cadence function in the article's recommended method?
features.detection_method: Identify whether recurring weekly, monthly, quarterly, daily, event-stage, or lifecycle timing is integral to the proposed method.

features.name: Explicit Numbering of Main Sections
features.question: Are main content units explicitly numbered as steps, tips, parts, reasons, or ranked entries?
features.detection_method: Check headings and lists for ordinal numbering that organizes the article's main body.

features.name: Action Verification Mechanism
features.question: How does the article tell readers to verify progress, correctness, or completion?
features.detection_method: Look for explicit success criteria, tests, measurement, review, validation, monitoring, or handoff.

features.name: New Material Introduced in Conclusion
features.question: Does the conclusion introduce a substantial new idea, framework, product, or recommendation not developed earlier?
features.detection_method: Compare the conclusion with prior sections and identify whether it adds rather than synthesizes.

features.name: Standalone Article Shell
features.question: Does the page function primarily as a self-contained article rather than a resource hub, landing page, or linked content ecosystem?
features.detection_method: Assess whether the reader can complete the article without depending on embedded resources, forms, linked modules, or external content.

features.name: Navigation and Page-Furniture Density
features.question: How much visible navigation, supplementary page furniture, or conversion scaffolding surrounds the article body?
features.detection_method: Rate visible use of tables of contents, links, author cards, related content, forms, downloads, subscriptions, videos, and conversion modules.

features.name: Qualification Density Placement
features.question: How are reader-specific qualifications incorporated into the article's navigable structure?
features.detection_method: Observe whether conditions are isolated, woven into guidance, or used to create visibly branching routes.

features.name: Dominant Knowledge Type
features.question: What main kind of knowledge work does the post perform?
features.detection_method: Identify the dominant intellectual task across the article: defining terms, explaining causes, teaching a process, comparing options, diagnosing conditions, presenting evidence, interpreting policy, framing strategy, or relaying a person's experience.

features.name: Assumed Reader Expertise
features.question: What level of prior domain knowledge does the post assume from its primary reader?
features.detection_method: Assess whether jargon is defined, basic concepts are introduced, setup steps are supplied, and advanced terminology is used without explanation.

features.name: Jargon Treatment
features.question: How does the article handle specialized terminology and acronyms?
features.detection_method: Sample specialized terms across the article and record whether they receive definitions, parenthetical glosses, examples, or no explanation.

features.name: Reader Role Framing
features.question: What role does the article assign to the reader during explanation?
features.detection_method: Inspect direct address, recommended actions, and implied responsibility for whether the reader is asked to learn, buy, operate, manage, evaluate, or occupy multiple roles.

features.name: Explanation-to-Action Ordering
features.question: How much explanation occurs before the first substantive recommendation?
features.detection_method: Locate the first recommendation that asks the reader to act and classify how much conceptual explanation precedes it.

features.name: Theory-to-Practice Bridge Form
features.question: How does the post convert explanation into reader implications?
features.detection_method: Look for formulations such as 'what this means,' 'therefore,' 'so you should,' or repeated explanation-to-action transitions.

features.name: Question Anticipation Level
features.question: How actively does the article pre-empt likely reader questions, objections, or uncertainties?
features.detection_method: Count rhetorical questions, objection-handling passages, FAQ headings, and explicit responses to likely reader concerns.

features.name: External Voice Integration
features.question: How are outside people or institutions incorporated into the explanatory argument?
features.detection_method: Check for named studies, regulators, standards, quotes, customer stories, interviews, or repeated external speakers.

features.name: Evidence Limitation Disclosure
features.question: Does the post explicitly disclose limits in its evidence, methods, date range, or applicability?
features.detection_method: Look for statements that a statistic is dated, a method is undisclosed, an example is illustrative, claims vary by context, or data has defined scope limits.

features.name: Product Role in Explanation
features.question: What role does a branded product or service play in the article's explanatory logic?
features.detection_method: Determine whether the brand is absent, incidental, illustrative, an enabling tool, the mechanism of the solution, a preferred winner, or the explicit endpoint.

features.name: Product Bridge Placement
features.question: Where does the product or service first enter the explanatory argument?
features.detection_method: Locate the first substantive brand/product mention and determine whether it recurs throughout.

features.name: Editorial-to-Commercial Separation
features.question: How clearly does the post separate educational explanation from its commercial recommendation?
features.detection_method: Assess whether product mentions are woven into explanation, appear lightly as context, arrive after editorial guidance, or occupy a visibly separate CTA section.

features.name: Definition Placement Pattern
features.question: Where are important terms primarily defined?
features.detection_method: Track first appearances of central terms and identify the dominant placement pattern.

features.name: Dominant Definition Form
features.question: How does the post most often define domain terms?
features.detection_method: Identify the most frequent form used when terms are introduced, such as direct definition, parenthesis, example, comparison, metaphor, or feature explanation.

features.name: Prerequisite Knowledge Supply
features.question: How does the post handle background knowledge needed to understand its recommendation?
features.detection_method: Determine whether needed background is explained in prose, provided through linked documentation or cited resources, outsourced entirely, or left unstated.

features.name: Definition Scope
features.question: What kinds of items does the article explicitly define?
features.detection_method: Mark each category for which the article gives an explicit definition, explanation, or first-use gloss.

features.name: Definition Reinforcement
features.question: After introducing a key term, does the article reinforce its meaning through repeated use, examples, or application?
features.detection_method: Check whether defined terms recur in later explanations, examples, headings, decision rules, or recommendations with consistent meaning.

features.name: Named Framework Use
features.question: Does the article organize explanation around an explicitly named framework, model, protocol, or set of pillars?
features.detection_method: Identify named constructs such as protocols, matrices, pillars, maturity models, diagnostic systems, or branded conceptual labels.

features.name: Framework Operationalization
features.question: How is the article's main framework converted into reader use?
features.detection_method: Determine whether the framework remains conceptual or becomes examples, criteria, conditional choices, or sequential steps.

features.name: Analogy Domain
features.question: What domain supplies the article's main teaching analogy or analogy system?
features.detection_method: Identify the recurring nonliteral comparison used to make the topic intelligible; choose no sustained analogy if metaphors are isolated rather than explanatory.

features.name: Mechanism Explanation Presence
features.question: Does the post explain why or how the recommended approach works?
features.detection_method: Assess whether causal, technical, behavioral, or system explanations merely justify advice or form the article's main content.

features.name: Operational Artifact Specificity
features.question: How specific are the concrete artifacts named in the explanation?
features.detection_method: Assess whether the post names only principles, generic actions, tool categories, specific settings or templates, or exact reproducible commands, fields, files, formulas, or scripts.

features.name: Dominant Mechanism Pattern
features.question: What type of explanatory relationship most often supports the post's claims?
features.detection_method: Identify the recurring relation used in explanatory sentences and section transitions.

features.name: Explanation Before First Recommendation
features.question: How much explanatory content appears before the first substantive recommendation or call to action?
features.detection_method: Locate the first directive, choice recommendation, or product recommendation, then assess how much explanatory setup precedes it.

features.name: Analogy Domain
features.question: What domain supplies the post's primary teaching analogy or explanatory metaphor?
features.detection_method: Identify the metaphorical source domain repeatedly used to make an abstract mechanism intelligible.

features.name: Theory-to-Practice Bridge Explicitness
features.question: How explicitly does the article translate explanation into practical implications?
features.detection_method: Look for phrases and moves such as 'this means,' 'therefore,' 'for your team,' 'in practice,' or immediate conversion of each mechanism into action.

features.name: First Recommendation Timing
features.question: How much explanation appears before the article gives its first substantive recommendation or instruction?
features.detection_method: Locate the first reader-directed recommendation beyond a generic promise or CTA and classify its position relative to explanatory setup.

features.name: Verification Mechanism
features.question: How does the article tell readers to know whether an action, diagnosis, or implementation worked?
features.detection_method: Identify stated success checks, including observation, metrics, test results, audits, validation gates, monitoring, or recurring review.

features.name: Ownership Assignment
features.question: Does the article specify who should perform, own, approve, or review recommended actions?
features.detection_method: Inspect recommendations for named actors, role allocation, handoffs, approval paths, escalation conditions, or cross-functional responsibilities.

features.name: Caveat Presence
features.question: Does the article explicitly state limitations, exclusions, contraindications, or conditions under which its guidance may not apply?
features.detection_method: Look for exclusions, exceptions, safety warnings, limitations, not-for-you statements, legal qualifications, or dependency conditions.

features.name: Caveat Placement
features.question: Where are caveats primarily placed in the article?
features.detection_method: Map caveat sentences to their article positions and identify the dominant placement pattern.

features.name: Comparison Presence and Scope
features.question: How does the article compare options, approaches, or states?
features.detection_method: Identify whether options are contrasted at all and whether comparison is simple, multi-option, audience-segmented, or systematically criterion-based.

features.name: Contraindication Specificity
features.question: How specifically does the post state who should not follow a recommendation or when an action should stop?
features.detection_method: Code exclusions, emergency conditions, eligibility limits, escalation triggers, and stop-use rules.

features.name: Comparison Presence
features.question: Does the post explicitly compare alternatives?
features.detection_method: Identify direct treatment of two or more options, approaches, product types, workflows, or strategic models.

features.name: Trade-off Explicitness
features.question: How explicitly does the post state costs or disadvantages of the preferred recommendation?
features.detection_method: Code whether the preferred path's costs, limits, risks, or implementation burdens are named and substantively weighed.

features.name: Recommendation Contestability
features.question: How does the post present its final preferred option?
features.detection_method: Assess whether the conclusion asserts one answer, qualifies it lightly, assigns choices by reader fit, preserves alternatives, or declines to prescribe.

features.name: Commercial Solution Separation
features.question: How is a branded product or service positioned relative to the educational explanation?
features.detection_method: Track whether branded capability is absent, contextual, illustrative, inseparable from the method, reserved for a closing CTA, or present throughout as the resolution.

features.name: External Authority Integration
features.question: What external authority form materially contributes to explanation?
features.detection_method: Select every authority type that is substantively used to explain, validate, or qualify the argument; select none only when no external authority appears.

features.name: Evidence Demonstration Mode
features.question: What proof modes does the post use to make explanations credible?
features.detection_method: Select all substantial proof modes used in the body; do not infer evidence from unsupported stylistic confidence.

features.name: Temporal Qualification Mode
features.question: How does the post handle the time sensitivity of its explanations and recommendations?
features.detection_method: Identify whether time is absent, operational, broadly current, historically anchored, dependent on dated facts, or mixed across sections.

features.name: Explanatory Format Aid
features.question: What non-prose or strongly modular format aid is used to reduce explanatory burden?
features.detection_method: Select all major aids that structure understanding beyond ordinary paragraphs and headings.

features.name: Safety or Professional Escalation Guidance
features.question: Does the post identify situations requiring professional review, emergency action, or specialist escalation?
features.detection_method: Look for explicit referral to clinicians, legal counsel, technicians, security specialists, financial advisors, or emergency/stop-use instructions.

features.name: Implementation Artifact Specificity
features.question: What concrete artifacts does the post ask readers to create, inspect, or use?
features.detection_method: Record all tangible artifacts named as part of execution, such as checklists, scripts, dashboards, logs, configurations, matrices, schedules, or contract language.

features.name: Validation and Feedback Loop Presence
features.question: Does the post instruct readers to validate results, monitor outcomes, or adjust the approach after implementation?
features.detection_method: Look for testing, monitoring, review, reconciliation, postmortems, dashboards, retesting, iteration, audits, or adjustment instructions.

features.name: Operational Granularity
features.question: How implementation-specific are the recommended actions?
features.detection_method: Assess whether readers receive only principles, named actions, conditions and parameters, or fully executable instructions with checks and artifacts.

features.name: Dominant Claim Support Mode
features.question: What is the predominant basis used to support consequential claims in the post?
features.detection_method: Identify the support mechanism used most often for central claims, excluding purely decorative examples and product mentions without a claim.

features.name: External Authority Presence
features.question: Does the post use at least one identifiable external authority to support a substantive claim?
features.detection_method: Mark present only when a named external person, organization, regulator, study, standard, customer, or public case supports a claim rather than appearing only as an unrelated example.

features.name: First-Party Proof Type
features.question: What first-party proof does the publisher use, if any?
features.detection_method: Mark all forms of publisher-controlled proof; do not count a generic claim that the brand is experienced unless experience is explicitly asserted.

features.name: Evidence Source Types Present
features.question: Which source types appear anywhere as support for claims?
values: reproducible code, calculation, table, or experiment
features.detection_method: Mark every listed source type visibly used to support a substantive claim, excluding passing mentions that do not bear argumentative weight.

features.name: Primary Authority Locus
features.question: Where does the article principally locate authority for its recommendations?
features.detection_method: Identify whose knowledge or credibility the article asks the reader to trust most when accepting its central recommendation.

features.name: External Voice Construction
features.question: How does the article incorporate voices beyond the main narrator?
values: repeated direct quotations from one source
interview or Q&A led by named expert
features.detection_method: Inspect quotation marks, attributed paraphrases, interview turns, bios, testimonials, and expert references across the article.

features.name: First-Party Proof Scope Disclosure
features.question: When first-party proof appears, how specifically does the article define its scope?
values: scope, time period, and method or population stated
features.detection_method: For publisher-originated claims, check whether the text gives a relevant use case, period, sample, customer population, data coverage, or method.

features.name: Illustrative Scenario Use
features.question: How are hypothetical or illustrative scenarios used as support?
values: used as primary proof of efficacy or magnitude
features.detection_method: Identify invented reader situations, example companies, sample calculations, or hypothetical incidents and assess their argumentative role.

features.name: Demonstrative Proof Presence
features.question: Does the article provide a reproducible or inspectable demonstration of a claim?
features.detection_method: Look for executable code, a complete calculation, a benchmark setup, a documented test procedure, a table of raw comparison inputs, or another artifact that a reader could replicate.

features.name: Numeric Density
features.question: How frequently does the post use numerical support in substantive claims?
features.detection_method: Count figures, percentages, ranges, time intervals, monetary values, thresholds, sample sizes, or measurement claims that support a claim rather than merely label a section.

features.name: Primary Number Function
features.question: What is the main argumentative role of numerical information in the post?
values: set an operational threshold or rule
features.detection_method: Classify the dominant function of figures, percentages, ranges, dates, counts, or calculated examples.

features.name: Number Precision Style
features.question: How are the post's substantive numbers generally expressed?
values: mix of rounded and exact figures
features.detection_method: Assess whether the predominant figures are rounded values, ranges, approximate markers such as 'about,' or exact-looking values with decimals or exact dates.

features.name: Baseline Disclosure for Comparative Numbers
features.question: When the post makes comparative numeric claims, does it state the comparison baseline?
features.detection_method: For claims such as faster, lower, higher, improved, or saved, check whether the prior state, comparator, or denominator is supplied.

features.name: Operational Threshold Use
features.question: Does the post turn one or more numeric values into an action trigger, eligibility rule, threshold, or decision boundary?
features.detection_method: Look for numbers tied to instructions such as wait times, limits, percentages, warning levels, budget triggers, sample windows, or escalation conditions.

features.name: Quantitative Claim Sourcing
features.question: How are the post's central numeric claims sourced?
values: mix of attributed and unattributed figures
most central figures identify a source
figures include source and methodological context
features.detection_method: Evaluate the main figures used to establish magnitude, efficacy, savings, risk, or comparison; dates alone do not count as central numeric claims.

features.name: Attribution Density
features.question: How frequently are substantive factual claims credited to identifiable sources?
features.detection_method: Assess attribution across factual, numerical, causal, and efficacy claims; exclude generic phrases such as 'experts say' unless the expert is identifiable.

features.name: Dominant Attribution Form
features.question: What attribution form is most prominent when the article credits evidence?
features.detection_method: Identify the most frequent or most rhetorically important form used to credit sources.

features.name: Citation Specificity
features.question: How specifically can a reader identify the source behind cited claims?
values: identifiable source with title, event, or date
features.detection_method: Check whether a skeptical reader could locate the underlying material using the details in the article.

features.name: Direct External Link Provision
features.question: Does the article provide direct external links to evidence, source material, regulator guidance, research, or documentation?
features.detection_method: Inspect hyperlinks or explicitly provided URLs that lead outside the publisher's own site to supporting material.

features.name: Reader Verification Ease
features.question: How easily could a skeptical reader independently verify the article's consequential factual claims?
features.detection_method: Rate 1 when claims are mostly anonymous or untraceable; rate 3 when some major claims identify sources; rate 5 when key claims have specific, accessible, traceable citations or reproducible artifacts.

features.name: Evidence Link Destination Type
features.question: Where do linked evidence or resource references primarily lead?
features.detection_method: Classify the primary destination type of links used near factual claims or evidence sections.

features.name: External Voice Diversity
features.question: How many distinct non-narrator authority voices materially contribute to the article?
values: two or more named outside voices
multiple distributed source types and voices
features.detection_method: Count materially used voices such as experts, regulators, researchers, customers, or interview participants; do not count passing brand names.

features.name: Methods Disclosure Level
features.question: How much does the post disclose about how evidence, data, testing, or comparison claims were produced?
values: reproducible method, data, or test conditions
features.detection_method: Look for sample, time period, source coverage, test environment, assumptions, inclusion criteria, process steps, or reproducible instructions.

features.name: Limits or Caveats Presence
features.question: Does the article explicitly state evidence limits, exceptions, exclusions, uncertainty, or circumstances where advice may not apply?
features.detection_method: Look for limitations such as jurisdiction dependence, eligibility conditions, incomplete methodology, atypical cases, contraindications, dated figures, or product-feature variability.

features.name: Causal Claim Calibration
features.question: How strongly does the post state causal or efficacy claims relative to the evidence it provides?
values: mixed hedged and assertive causal language
assertive causal claims with limited support
absolute causal or efficacy claims with no visible support
features.detection_method: Compare wording such as may, can, associated with, helps, drives, prevents, guarantees, or will against the cited evidence and disclosed methods.

features.name: Causal Claim Strength
features.question: How strongly does the post claim that an intervention, product, or condition causes an outcome?
features.detection_method: Identify the strongest causal language used, including may, can, helps, leads to, drives, prevents, ensures, or will.

features.name: Primary Evidentiary Purpose
features.question: What is the central thing evidence is asked to prove in the article?
values: justify a protocol or operating threshold
features.detection_method: Assess the role evidence plays in advancing the main conclusion, not merely the topic of the evidence.

features.name: Evidence Purpose
features.question: What does the article's most prominent evidence item attempt to establish?
values: credibility of the publisher or product
features.detection_method: Identify the claim immediately supported by the article's most prominent statistic, citation, quote, case, demonstration, or authority reference.

features.name: First-Party Claim Scope
features.question: When the publisher makes a first-party performance or experience claim, does it define the claim's scope?
values: scope limited by use case or customer type
scope limited by timeframe or date
scope limited by method or conditions
scope limited by multiple contextual qualifiers
features.detection_method: Inspect brand claims for stated population, timeframe, setup, product tier, operational condition, or use-case boundaries.

features.name: Evidence-to-Claim Placement
features.question: How is evidence generally sequenced around the claims it supports?
values: evidence clustered in a separate proof section
features.detection_method: Inspect section and sentence order to determine whether support precedes, follows, is integrated with, or is separated from the claim.

features.name: Evidence Transparency Score
features.question: Overall, how transparent is the post about where its consequential claims come from and what their limits are?
values: 4 - clear sources or methods with limits
features.detection_method: Holistically assess attribution specificity, methods, scope, limitations, source accessibility, and reproducibility for consequential claims.

features.name: Testing or Validation Instruction
features.question: Does the post instruct the reader to validate a claim, configuration, choice, or outcome before relying on it?
features.detection_method: Mark present when the text directs readers to run a test, pilot, benchmark, audit, compare outcomes, monitor metrics, use a checklist, or verify a result.

features.name: Reader-Generated Measurement Prompt
features.question: Does the article ask readers to calculate, test, track, audit, or benchmark their own situation?
features.detection_method: Look for instructions to measure time, calculate ratios, run a test, inspect logs, compare prices, track trends, or evaluate a threshold.

features.name: Primary Voice Identity
features.question: Who is the dominant speaking persona for the main body of the post?
features.detection_method: Identify the persona that makes the main claims, frames recommendations, and controls the conclusion; use bylines, first-person claims, editorial framing, and speaker labels.

features.name: Institutional Self-Reference Mode
features.question: How does the post invoke the publishing organization as a speaking position?
features.detection_method: Look for statements such as 'we have seen,' 'our customers,' 'our platform,' organizational experience claims, and first-person brand assertions in the body.

features.name: Main Voice Stability
features.question: How stable is the main speaking position across the post?
features.detection_method: Compare opening, central explanatory sections, quoted material, and conclusion for changes in speaker identity or authority posture.

features.name: Authorial Advocacy Intensity
features.question: How strongly does the main narrator advocate a preferred model, platform, or behavior?
features.detection_method: Assess evaluative wording, binary contrasts, imperative language, dismissal of alternatives, and whether the conclusion presents one preferred path as necessary.

features.name: Main Voice Persona
features.question: What functional persona does the main voice adopt toward the reader?
features.detection_method: Classify the dominant rhetorical role: teaching execution, analyzing strategy, helping selection, explaining editorially, advocating change, selling a solution, or asking interview questions.

features.name: Secondary Voice Count
features.question: How many distinct secondary voices appear beyond the primary narrator?
features.detection_method: Count distinct named people, organizations speaking through attributed statements, customer cases, testimonials, or sustained hypothetical stakeholder voices.

features.name: Floor Control
features.question: Who receives the greatest share of discursive space in a multi-voice article?
features.detection_method: Compare paragraph volume, quotation length, turn count, and whether the narrator summarizes versus relays other speakers.

features.name: Direct Quotation Presence
features.question: Does the article include direct quotations attributable to someone other than the main narrator?
features.detection_method: Look for quotation marks or transcript turns attributed to experts, customers, leaders, employees, regulators, or other external speakers.

features.name: Quotation Prominence
features.question: What structural role do direct quotations play?
features.detection_method: Assess whether quotations are absent, incidental, repeated evidence, section-organizing devices, or the main article format.

features.name: Source Placement Pattern
features.question: Where are secondary voices or source references concentrated?
features.detection_method: Map each attributed voice, reference, or case to opening, body, and conclusion sections.

features.name: Secondary Voice Forms
features.question: What forms do secondary voices take?
features.detection_method: Mark every represented form, distinguishing actual attributed people from invented scenarios and sample language.

features.name: Named Expert Voice Use
features.question: How is a named individual expert used, if at all?
features.detection_method: Check bylines, bios, quotations, Q&A labels, and repeated attribution to determine the expert's actual speaking role.

features.name: Voice Floor Control
features.question: Who receives the greatest substantive textual space in a multi-voice post?
features.detection_method: Estimate relative word count and argumentative control across narrator prose, quotations, transcript turns, and case material.

features.name: Authorial Framing of Secondary Voices
features.question: How does the main narrator handle secondary voices?
features.detection_method: Examine text before and after quotations or attributed material for interpretation, agreement, qualification, challenge, or minimal mediation.

features.name: Dominant Credibility Basis
features.question: What is the article's primary method for establishing credibility?
features.detection_method: Determine which credibility device is most central to why the reader should trust the article's recommendations.

features.name: Attribution Transparency
features.question: How transparently does the article identify the origin of its factual or expert claims?
features.detection_method: Assess citations, links, publication names, report titles, dates, DOI-style references, named datasets, and source locators.

features.name: Proprietary Authority Claim
features.question: Does the article use proprietary platform access, internal data, customer scale, or product capability as proof?
features.detection_method: Mark present when claims rely on the company's dashboard, customer base, product telemetry, service history, platform functionality, or internal observations.

features.name: External Authority Diversity
features.question: How many distinct kinds of external authority are used materially?
features.detection_method: Count distinct authority classes used substantively: regulators, journals, standards bodies, analysts, universities, associations, named public cases, or expert professionals.

features.name: Attribution Specificity
features.question: How specifically are external claims or authorities attributed?
features.detection_method: Assess the most specific attribution level used for factual, expert, or performance claims.

features.name: External Authority Types
features.question: What types of external authority are invoked?
features.detection_method: Mark each external authority type explicitly named or clearly invoked in the article.

features.name: Primary Reader Role
features.question: What role does the article primarily assign to the reader?
features.detection_method: Infer the role from verbs, tasks, questions, and the kind of agency the article asks the reader to exercise.

features.name: Second-Person Address Density
features.question: How frequently does the article directly address the reader as 'you' or through equivalent imperatives?
features.detection_method: Scan body sections for direct second-person pronouns, direct questions, and imperative clauses addressed to the reader.

features.name: Reader Address Mode
features.question: What is the dominant rhetorical mode of reader address?
features.detection_method: Identify whether the reader is mainly informed, told what to do, asked to diagnose themselves, challenged to change, reassured, or invited toward a service.

features.name: Reader Self-Assessment Device
features.question: What self-assessment device is offered to the reader?
features.detection_method: Look for questions, decision rules, checklists, thresholds, scoring systems, matrices, or side-by-side evaluation structures.

features.name: Reader Agency Scope
features.question: What level of action is the reader expected to undertake?
features.detection_method: Determine the highest level of action explicitly expected from the reader in the article's recommendations.

features.name: Reader Expertise Assumption
features.question: What level of prior expertise does the article assume of its primary reader?
features.detection_method: Assess unexplained terminology, prerequisite knowledge, technical detail, and whether foundational concepts are defined.

features.name: Reader Participation Invitation Presence
features.question: Does the post explicitly invite the reader to take part beyond silently reading?
features.detection_method: Look for invitations to comment, ask a question, self-assess, use a tool, attend, contact, subscribe, join, download, or complete a task.

features.name: Commercial CTA Explicitness
features.question: How explicit is the post's commercial next-step request?
features.detection_method: Assess whether the post merely mentions a brand, links to education, invites contact or demo, or directly instructs a purchase, signup, download, or application.

features.name: Participation Invitation Placement
features.question: Where is the strongest reader invitation placed?
features.detection_method: Locate explicit requests to act, contact, register, test, download, subscribe, comment, purchase, or consult someone.

features.name: Task Closure Style
features.question: How does the article close the reader's assigned task?
features.detection_method: Classify the final substantive paragraph or CTA by whether it summarizes, recommends, gives steps, prompts evaluation, refers to professionals, sells, or routes to resources/community.

features.name: Commercial CTA Intensity
features.question: How commercially direct is the article's strongest next step?
features.detection_method: Assess the closing and any prominent in-body invitations for contact, demo, purchase, signup, booking, or application language.

features.name: External Participation Pathway
features.question: Does the article route readers beyond the article through a participation or resource mechanism?
features.detection_method: Check for links or explicit routes to demos, documentation, tools, videos, case studies, webinars, newsletters, communities, support resources, or purchase pages.

features.name: Speaking Format
features.question: What is the article's dominant speaking arrangement?
features.detection_method: Identify whether prose is primarily authored narration, organized around quotations, speaker turns, transcript exchanges, recap units, cases, or source-specific list entries.

features.name: Secondary Voice Count
features.question: How many distinct secondary human or institutional voices appear beyond the main narrator?
features.detection_method: Count distinct named people, organizations speaking through attributed claims, customer cases, regulators, or recurring personas; exclude unlabeled generic examples.

features.name: Secondary Voice Entry Mode
features.question: How do secondary voices primarily enter the text?
features.detection_method: Classify the dominant way non-narrator perspectives appear. If more than one form occurs, select the form that receives the greatest textual emphasis.

features.name: Author Floor Control
features.question: Who controls the greatest share of explanatory space and interpretive framing?
features.detection_method: Compare the amount of authored exposition with quoted, transcript, or case-speaker material and note whether the narrator interprets or merely relays it.

features.name: Source Interruption Pattern
features.question: When other voices appear, how does the main author handle them?
features.detection_method: Inspect the paragraphs surrounding quotes, testimonies, cases, or expert turns to determine whether the author absorbs, interprets, relays, or contrasts them.

features.name: Named Expert Structural Role
features.question: What role does a named expert play in the article, if one appears?
features.detection_method: Identify whether a named expert is merely mentioned, quoted once, repeatedly quoted, interviewed, or positioned as the principal authorial authority.

features.name: Overall Guidance Level
features.question: What is the highest sustained level of executable guidance provided by the post?
features.detection_method: Assess whether the article merely explains, recommends actions, lists actionable items, provides ordered steps, or supplies an end-to-end implementation system with roles, controls, and follow-up.

features.name: Dominant Action Structure
features.question: How are the article's main actions structurally organized?
features.detection_method: Identify whether actions are isolated suggestions, scannable checklist items, ordered steps, phases of adoption, if-then choices, or actions attached to individual cases or profiles.

features.name: Visible Step Labeling
features.question: How are actionable units visibly labeled in the post?
features.detection_method: Inspect headings and formatting for numbered steps, phases, tips, questions, bullets, matrices, or prose-only actions.

features.name: Numbered Procedure Presence
features.question: Does the article present any principal guidance as explicitly numbered steps, phases, or stages?
features.detection_method: Mark yes when headings or body text explicitly enumerate a procedure using numbered steps, phases, parts, or stages.

features.name: Action Granularity
features.question: At what level of granularity are the post's actions usually expressed?
features.detection_method: Compare statements like 'improve governance' or 'audit your process' with tasks such as 'export a CSV' and configuration instructions such as setting a threshold, field, duration, or permission.

features.name: Decision Rule Presence
features.question: Does the post give explicit criteria for choosing among actions, tools, or paths?
features.detection_method: Identify explicit fit language such as if, unless, when, based on, choose X for Y, avoid X if Y, or eligibility requirements.

features.name: Implementation Lifecycle Coverage
features.question: Which lifecycle stages are covered by the article's guidance?
features.detection_method: Select every lifecycle stage explicitly addressed through action guidance. Do not infer stages from background explanation alone.

features.name: Action-to-Explanation Balance
features.question: How much of the post consists of executable guidance rather than explanation, argument, or background?
features.detection_method: Estimate the proportion of paragraphs, bullets, tables, scripts, or sections that tell the reader what to do versus explain why.

features.name: Primary Actor Expected to Act
features.question: Who is primarily expected to perform the article's recommended actions?
features.detection_method: Identify the actor addressed by imperatives and responsibility statements, such as the reader, manager, team, organization, vendor, clinician, lawyer, or consultant.

features.name: Actor Model
features.question: How many distinct actor types are required for the recommended method?
features.detection_method: Map the actors necessary to execute the post's method, including managers, peers, operators, vendors, product teams, clinicians, lawyers, or service professionals.

features.name: Escalation Ownership
features.question: Does the post specify who should take over when the initial actor cannot safely or effectively proceed?
features.detection_method: Look for instructions to contact a manager, vendor, support team, mechanic, clinician, attorney, regulator, or emergency service, including stop-work or stop-use directions.

features.name: Instructional Concreteness Markers
features.question: What concrete execution markers appear in the article's guidance?
features.detection_method: Select each marker explicitly used in actionable instruction, not merely mentioned in background context.

features.name: Numerical Operational Specificity
features.question: How are numbers used in the article's action guidance?
features.detection_method: Distinguish illustrative examples from recommended ranges, fixed targets, explicit thresholds, and articles using multiple numeric control forms.

features.name: Timing Specificity
features.question: What type of timing instruction supports the recommended actions?
features.detection_method: Identify whether timing is vague urgency, recurring cadence, a wait duration, a calendar date or deadline, an event trigger, or several of these.

features.name: Artifact Production Requirement
features.question: Does the guidance require the reader to create, collect, update, or submit a tangible operational artifact?
features.detection_method: Mark yes for required artifacts such as a checklist, CSV, report, dashboard, chart, script, contract, log, template, inventory, or documented plan.

features.name: Effort Framing
features.question: How does the article frame the effort required to execute its recommendations?
features.detection_method: Look for stated time, money, staffing, skill level, complexity, implementation burden, or comparisons of effort.

features.name: Named Tool Specificity
features.question: What level of tool specificity appears in the instructions?
features.detection_method: Identify whether instructions mention only categories, named products, named features, or exact commands, APIs, flags, menus, file names, or interface controls.

features.name: Quantification Type
features.question: What forms of quantification are used in actionable instructions?
features.detection_method: Mark every applicable type of number used as an instruction, threshold, target, dose, timing, scale marker, or budget criterion.

features.name: Scripted Language Availability
features.question: Does the post supply words the reader can use verbatim?
features.detection_method: Identify quoted phrases, sample replies, negotiation lines, customer messages, emails, or dialogue scripts intended for direct reuse.

features.name: Timing Specificity
features.question: How specifically does the post attach timing to actions?
features.detection_method: Check for vague urgency, first/next sequencing, weekly/monthly cycles, or exact periods such as 48 hours, day three, 90 days, Q4, 24-hour response, or 7 DPO.

features.name: Effort Framing
features.question: How does the post frame the effort required to execute the guidance?
features.detection_method: Identify stated or implied time, complexity, staffing, budget, implementation burden, rollout duration, or recurring-management requirement.

features.name: Technical Detail Level
features.question: How technically detailed are the instructions?
features.detection_method: Assess whether the post remains general, names practical processes, uses domain vocabulary, specifies settings/mechanisms, or includes code, formulas, protocols, or specialist-level controls.

features.name: Conditional Logic Presence
features.question: Does the post provide explicit conditions for choosing among actions?
features.detection_method: Look for if, when, unless, depending on, based on, only if, avoid if, or comparable decision criteria tied to different recommendations.

features.name: Conditional Logic Complexity
features.question: What is the most complex form of conditional logic used in the post?
features.detection_method: Assess whether the article has one simple rule, multiple separate rules, a binary choice, a multi-variable fit model, or a loop in which results determine the next action.

features.name: Decision Criterion Basis
features.question: What kind of information most often determines the recommended choice?
features.detection_method: Identify the conditions used to route advice, such as goals, revenue, team size, health status, platform environment, compliance requirements, risk, or observed data.

features.name: Fit Recommendation Style
features.question: How does the post express fit between reader conditions and recommended options?
features.detection_method: Look for generic recommendations versus 'best for,' 'not for,' comparison tables, self-assessments, eligibility screens, or diagnostic questions before advice.

features.name: Trade-off Disclosure
features.question: How does the post handle drawbacks, costs, or conditions under which its recommendation may not fit?
features.detection_method: Assess whether caveats are absent, vague, specific, balanced across options, or used to route readers to a different solution or professional handoff.

features.name: Success Verification Design
features.question: How does the post tell the reader to verify that an action worked?
features.detection_method: Look for expected results, checks, before/after measures, audit criteria, test outputs, dashboards, monitoring, or review cycles.

features.name: Repetition and Review Loop
features.question: Does the post prescribe repeated review, iteration, or continuous improvement?
features.detection_method: Identify recurring reviews, reassessments, retrospectives, monthly checks, optimization loops, recurring audits, or ongoing measurement.

features.name: Feedback Source
features.question: What feedback source is used to adjust actions over time?
features.detection_method: Mark each feedback source that the post says should inform adjustment, optimization, escalation, or next decisions.

features.name: Verification Method
features.question: What is the strongest verification method provided for recommended actions?
features.detection_method: Identify whether success is judged by feeling, observation, a metric, a test, an audit, or validation by a clinician, attorney, vendor, technician, or reviewer.

features.name: Resource Provision Type
